title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Villarreal: Reds Recover From Disastrous Start
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:14 PM EDTAlexis Mac Allister (left) scored twice in Liverpool’s victory. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLiverpool overcame a wretched start to Tuesday’s Champions League encounter with Villarreal and claimed a 4–3 victory over the Yellow Submarine on Matchday 3 of the league phase.
The very worst of Andoni Iraola’s Reds manifested in the opening 35 minutes, as a Villarreal side familiar with Iraola’s ideals took full advantage of a team struggling to perform as instructed.

A Virgil van Dijk mistake was seized upon superbly by Georges Mikautadze after four minutes, and Iñigo Pérez’s visitors ventured toward dreamland on Merseyside when unlikely goalscorer Sergi Cardona doubled their advantage just before the half-hour mark.

Liverpool’s resurgence was crucially ignited before things worsened, and Alexis Mac Allister’s leap from Kostas Tsimikas immediately brought them back into the game. Cardona then cancelled out his strike at the other end by allowing Ronald Araújo to equalize at the back post, meaning the hosts boasted all the momentum entering the second half.

And Iraola’s side suddenly performed with newfound control with the contest level. Their assurance evolved into a final-third spurt, as Mac Allister scored his second and Florian Wirtz opened the floodgates. It seemed like a procession, but Tani Oluwaseyi’s late strike set up a nervy conclusion from nowhere.

Liverpool were terrible without the ball early on. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesIraola was up against a very familiar face in Iñigo Pérez, who was his assistant at Rayo Vallecano and was set to join him at Bournemouth, only to be denied a work permit.
The Liverpool manager said Pérez “knows everything” about him, and it certainly looked as if the apprentice had all the answers to the test at Anfield.

Iraola is defined by his work out of possession, and his Liverpool team is a work in progress. It was evident before Brentford went down to 10 at the weekend, and even more distinct during the opening 35 minutes on Tuesday evening. Pérez’s Villarreal rotated freely in a bid to disorient Liverpool’s man-to-man pressure, and the technical level of the visitors meant they seized upon the Reds’ confusion without the ball.

Villarreal’s second goal typified just how poor Liverpool were to begin this match, with a litany of players late to assignments as the Yellow Submarine went from back to front. Left back Sergi Cardona burst in behind to finish past Alisson.

At that moment, the Anfield faithful feared the worst. Fortunately, Iraola’s facilitation of chaos helped them back into the contest, and the control they asserted after the restart, with the match suddenly all square, showcased their volatility. We saw two completely different Liverpool teams on Tuesday.
Mac Allister’s header got Liverpool going. / Liverpool FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—5.7: Won’t be happy, given the three concessions. Issues laid ahead of him.

RB: Ronald Araújo—7.4: The Uruguayan scored in successive Champions League games, creeping in at the back post to head home from Rio’s teasing delivery left by goalscorer Cardona. Withdrawn at halftime.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—6.5: An imperfect showing from the gifted Frenchman. Jacquet was unnerved by Villarreal’s directness early on.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—5.5: No one was more relieved by Liverpool’s fightback than their captain, whose error directly led to Villarreal’s opening goal. There was much to dislike about the Reds’ display in the opening 35 minutes, and Van Dijk typified their shoddiness.
LB: Kostas Tsimikas—8.4: Few would argue that the Greek international boasts the requisite quality. Still, his set-piece delivery helped Liverpool back into the game.

CM: Trey Nyoni—7.9: There’s plenty for Nyoni to improve without the ball, but he’s ever so easy on the eye in possession. Performs like a mini-Gravenberch, given his ability to resist and roll past pressure.

CM: Alexis Mac Allister—9.3: The Argentine’s best work so far this term has arrived in this competition. Mac Allister’s header inspired his team, and he crashed the box brilliantly to hand Liverpool the advantage after the hour mark.

RW: Rio Ngumoha—8.9: This was a definitive showing from the teenager, who’s had a relatively slow start to the season. Rio is blessed with the skill set of a seasoned winger, and that came to the fore majestically on a sodden Anfield field. Villarreal couldn’t cope with the youngster’s ebullience.
